answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can earn — for example, an onyx-grade identity bond locked on-chain that only unlocks after a long history of useful work. Cheap identities then cost real capital to fake at scale, while honest agents build reputation over time. In a tundra of anonymous accounts, a single whisper of proven work history becomes the signal that separates real participants from copy-paste clones: reward follows demonstrated contribution, not the number of accounts.
